messages:
maria: Heads-up — since ~03:10 UTC apac-2 is churning allocations between warm-pool and preemptible. Tail latency and KV cache regen are spiking (x3) and some tenants see repeated cold-starts. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/gpu/apac-2 :eyes:
opsbot: alert triggered: 03:11 UTC — slice.apac-2 churn-rate > 2.5/min, kv-regen-rate 620/s. Notified #eng-infra.
sam: any recent scheduler/placement changes rolled out to apac?
maria: not from our side — small rollout to allocation-balancer yesterday (canary) but target was eu/na only. still, behaviors line up with egress bursts causing slab evictions.
liam: I saw similar pattern last month when NIC queue saturation caused nvlink backpressure -> slab churn. Can someone grab node-level NIC/NV counters and pcie errs?
hana: quick mitigation option: soft-shield the hottest tenant cohort into a fractional dedicated slice for 15m to reduce cross-tenant noise. Command: ```redwoodctl pool shield --slice apac-2 --tenants tenant_ids=tz-prod,search-prod --duration 15m --mode soft --priority high```
maria: running that now against tz-prod + search-prod. Will post outcome in 2-3m.
opsbot: action scheduled: soft-shield started at 03:14 UTC (id=shield-1765550000-1).
maria: quick paste of node probe around 03:12 — nvlink rx errors ticked, nic tx drops ~500/min on 3 hosts:```
node-87 gpu0: nvlink_rx_errors=12 nvlink_tx_errors=0 nic_tx_drops=512
node-88 gpu1: nvlink_rx_errors=9 nic_tx_drops=478
node-91 gpu0: nvlink_rx_errors=0 nic_tx_drops=0```
sam: ok that looks like a network egress microspike hitting certain racks. Is it tied to an external export job or tenant heavy batch?
liam: run a flowlog correlate: `kquery flowlogs "dst=egress AND slice=apac-2" | top 20 by bytes @ 03:00..03:15` — if we see a tenant streaming model checkpoints or large evals that's the culprit.
maria: flowlogs show heavy egress from tz-prod -> s3 (multipart upload) starting 03:05. That explains NVLINK contention when host tries to flush.
hana: for immediate relief we can 1) keep soft-shield for 30m, 2) add per-tenant egress policer (10Gb cap) for tz-prod, 3) flag this tenant for billing/ops to schedule checkpoint windows. Which of those should I wire up?
sam: do 1+2 now. Create billing ticket after. Also capture perf trace for a couple of the cold-started requests for regression eval.
maria: soft-shield extended to 30m. opsbot scheduled egress policer: `redwoodctl net limit --tenant tz-prod --slice apac-2 --egress 10g` — started 03:18 UTC.
opsbot: policy applied: egress cap=10G for tenant=tz-prod on slice=apac-2 (id=pol-1765550000-2).
liam: long term: we should consider isolating long-tail egress workloads into an "egress-dedicated" pool per region (fractional dedicated) or tighten our egress-aware placement scoring in the allocator. Also bump warm-pool KV cache grace to reduce regen churn on transient evictions.
sam: Agreed. I'll create RFC for: "egress-dedicated fractional pools + allocator egress penalty" and include cost estimate and impact on capacity.
hana: I'll own the short-term playbook updates and add the shield + policer steps to the runbook.
maria: after shield + policer, observed kv-regen drop from 620/s -> 70/s and cold-starts fell to baseline within 2min. Keeping monitoring for 15m. thanks all :thumbsup:
opsbot: incident resolved (degraded->ok) at 03:22 UTC. Reminder: follow up RFC and billing ticket required.
